distractors.reason: We don't say 'look at the bus' to mean waiting. 'Look at' means to direct your eyes toward something you can see.
We don't say 'listen to the bus' to mean waiting. 'Listen to' is used with sounds, music or speech.
We don't say 'ask about the bus' to mean waiting. 'Ask about' means requesting information or asking a question.

example_sentence: Every morning I ___ the bus at the corner near my house.
l1_interference: Українською ми кажемо «чекати на автобус», тому легко подумати, що «wait» завжди потребує прийменника так само, як українське «на». В англійській правильно «wait for», а не «wait the bus» без прийменника.
explanation: In English, 'wait' is followed by 'for' when you are expecting a person, vehicle or event to arrive. The preposition 'for' is part of the verb partnership and cannot be left out.

related_collocations.example: I always look for my keys before I leave home.
We listen to music on the bus.
The shop opens early, so we depend on the first bus.

memory_tip: WAIT FOR = stay until someone or something arrives | LOOK AT = direct your eyes at something you can see
